/-!
# Littlewood conjectures

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Littlewood_conjecture)
- [Bernard de Mathan and Olivier Teulié, *Problèmes diophantiens simultanés*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00605-003-0199-y)
-/

open Filter

-- TODO(mercuris): This is a norm on ℝ/ℤ, show this?

namespace LittlewoodConjecture


/--
For any two real numbers $\alpha$ and $\beta$,
$$
  \liminf_{n\to\infty} n\||n\alpha\||\||n\beta\|| = 0
$$
where $\||x\|| := \min(|x - \lfloor x \rfloor|, |x - \lceil x \rceil|)$ is the distance
to the nearest integer.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem littlewood_conjecture (α β : ℝ) :
    atTop.liminf (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ n * distToNearestInt (n * α) * distToNearestInt (n * β)) = 0 := by
  sorry

/--
For real number $\alpha$ and prime $p$,
$$
  \liminf\_{n \to\infty} n |n|\_{p}\||n\alpha\|| = 0
$$
where $\||x\|| := \min(|x - \lfloor x \rfloor|, |x - \lceil x \rceil|)$ is the distance
to the nearest integer, and $|x|\_{p}$ is the $p$-adic norm.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem padic_littlewood_conjecture (α : ℝ) (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) :
    atTop.liminf (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ n * padicNorm p n * distToNearestInt (n * α)) = 0 := by
  sorry

end LittlewoodConjecture

reformulations.difference: Lean uses a real-valued limit inferior over ℕ, matching Wikipedia. Bugeaud’s survey instead uses the equivalent infimum over positive integers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Write f(n)=n‖nα‖‖nβ‖. It is nonnegative, and Dirichlet approximation together with ‖x‖≤1/2 gives arbitrarily large n with f(n)≤1/2, so Lean’s real liminf has its ordinary meaning rather than a default value. If a positive-index term vanishes, either nα or nβ is an integer, and all positive multiples of that index also give zero. Otherwise every finite positive-index prefix has a strictly positive minimum, so infimum zero forces arbitrarily late terms below every ε>0. The converse is immediate. The equivalence and the boundedness argument were proved in /workspace/review/liminf_checks.lean without sorryAx.

reformulations.difference: Wikipedia and Bugeaud state an infimum over positive integers; Lean uses a real-valued limit inferior over ℕ. Einsiedler–Kleinbock explicitly give this limit-inferior formulation as well.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For prime p, f(n)=n|n|ₚ‖nα‖ is nonnegative. Along n=p^k, n|n|ₚ=1, hence f(n)≤1/2; these indices tend to infinity, preventing any real-liminf default-value issue. A zero at a positive index implies nα is an integer, so zeros occur at all multiples of that index. If no positive-index term vanishes, finite prefixes have positive minima, and infimum zero therefore forces arbitrarily late terms below every ε>0. Conversely, such arbitrarily late small terms imply infimum zero. Including n=0 does not affect the limit inferior. The exact equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/liminf_checks.lean without sorryAx.

review.notes: Both declarations were verified. Lean checks confirmed the quantifiers and coercions, the equality of distToNearestInt with both nearest-integer characterizations, and the harmlessness of n=0. Boundary tests covered integer and signed fractional inputs, half-integer ties, p=2, exclusion of p=0 and p=1, and computed p-adic norms for small integers. Experiments are in /workspace/review/scratch.lean and /workspace/review/liminf_checks.lean. Although the original Springer article was inaccessible beyond its abstract, Einsiedler–Kleinbock explicitly state and attribute the relevant conjecture. Both research-open tags agree with the current Wikipedia source.
